# Database normalisation

## Normal forms

Normalisation organises a relational database to reduce redundancy and prevent update anomalies. A table is in first normal form when every column holds a single atomic value. A table is in second normal form when it is in first normal form and every non-key column depends on the whole primary key. A table is in third normal form when it is in second normal form and no non-key column depends on another non-key column.

## Trade-offs

Normalised designs need more joins to answer queries that span several tables. Some systems denormalise selected tables on purpose to make frequent reads faster. Denormalisation increases redundancy, so the application must keep the copies consistent.
